concerns_updated.new_author_response: Authors clarified akinetic episodes were NOT excluded — they were included in the competition dataset and labeled as kinetic/akinetic in events.csv, but the contest scoring was not tied to those labels. Added Supplementary methods describing the kinetic/akinetic annotations and now report the percentage of FOG episodes labeled akinetic. Events where annotators could not decide between akinetic FOG vs voluntary stop were marked non-valid in the Valid column.

Authors acknowledged the single-center cohort limitation and the lack of an independent validation cohort. They explained TCGA is not usable for validation — only 14 pediatric thyroid cases (all >14 yr) with no recurrence information. They argued protein-mRNA correlation <60% means adult/mRNA datasets are not directly transposable, and committed to future prospective multicenter clinical trials. No new external validation was added in revision.

Worklist labels this as Reviewer #1 but the matching concern in the PDF is Reviewer #4 comment 4 (factors affecting infection/vaccination differentiation). Authors added limitations paragraph (Line 345) acknowledging humoral variability, childhood smallpox immunization as confounder, and ATI-N-CPXV time-decay. Demonstrated robustness via: (i) testing on acute + epidemiological panels, (ii) independent validation cohort (n=143), (iii) analyzing childhood vaccination dependence, (iv) breakthrough infection assessment, (v) ATI-N as MVA vs MPXV differentiator. No additional clade-specific testing performed.

Authors restructured the manuscript around generalization across multiple external datasets (SHHS1, SHHS2, UHV, CFS, MROS, MESA — diverse populations, ethnicities, ages, sex, comorbidities). Removed the transfer learning experiment and renamed the model OxiNet. Harmonized AHI scoring to AASM12 rule (confirmed with NSSR administrators). Removed SHHS1-training patients from SHHS2 test set to avoid leakage. Reported ICC 0.92-0.96 and F1 0.75-0.84 with bootstrap 95% CIs and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests vs ODI/OBM baselines (p<0.05 all databases).
